title: Email Draft
description: Draft clear, well-structured professional emails for common situations with appropriate tone and call to action.
template:
Draft a professional email for [SITUATION, e.g. "requesting a deadline extension" / "introducing yourself to a new team" / "sending a follow-up after a meeting"].

Recipient: [ROLE OR PERSON]

Tone: [FORMAL / FRIENDLY-PROFESSIONAL / DIRECT / EMPATHETIC]

Key points to include:
- [POINT 1]
- [POINT 2]
- [POINT 3]

Desired outcome: [WHAT YOU WANT THE RECIPIENT TO DO NEXT]

Constraints or context: [E.G. THIS IS THE FIRST CONTACT / KEEP IT SHORT / REFER TO PREVIOUS CONVERSATION]

Please provide:
- A complete subject line
- A polished email body
- A brief explanation of why the tone and structure were chosen
example:
Draft a professional email for requesting a deadline extension.

Recipient: Project manager

Tone: EMPATHETIC

Key points to include:
- I need two more days for the draft
- The delay will not block the next milestone
- I will share a revised timeline shortly

Desired outcome: Approval for the extension and updated timeline acknowledgment

Constraints or context: Keep it concise and avoid over-explaining

Please provide:
- A complete subject line
- A polished email body
- A brief explanation of why the tone and structure were chosen
tips: State the ask in the first paragraph so busy readers understand immediately
Include the deadline and new date in the subject line when possible
Offer one clear next step to make responding easy
